prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map depicts a top-down indoor floor layout where the camera wearer sits or crouches looking downward at a tiled floor about 0.8 to 1.0 m away, with a glass door or window in the upper right at roughly 1.2 to 1.5 m. The wearer's own arms, thighs, and held hacksaw in the lower foreground are brightest and closest (0.2 to 0.5 m, within immediate arm's reach), positioned above a flat wooden board (around 0.8 m away), while a blue hot-glue gun, a white open-topped wooden box, a tall white cardboard tube, a dark cylinder, a ball of twine, and a cat lie roughly 0.2 to 0.6 m apart from one another across the floor at 0.7 to 1.3 m depth. Across the five frames, the wearer's left arm advances into the lower-left view in frame 2 to hold a small vertical wooden piece on the board while the right hand saws it in frames 2–4 before retreating to the bottom-left in frame 5, and meanwhile the cat in the upper right walks rightward (frames 1–4) and turns upward toward the glass door in frame 5, facing away from the camera wearer throughout. The depth map clearly reveals the 3D vertical protrusion of the tilted cardboard tube, the upright wooden box walls, and the elevated angle of the hacksaw frame above the flat board, which are harder to judge from the overhead RGB angle alone. However, the depth map is unreliable around the thin hacksaw blade (which disappears into the background depth in frames 1–3), the bright sunlit glass door in frame 1 (which renders pitch-black as if infinitely far), and the upper-right window area in frames 4–5 where the cat's body and bright sunlit door frame are falsely assigned very bright near-field depth values.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates only a few foreground elements against a black background: the camera wearer's lower arms and legs at 0.2 to 0.6 m in the bottom foreground (within arm's reach), the held hacksaw frame above the wooden board at 0.3 to 0.6 m, and the cat in the upper right at roughly 1.0 to 1.3 m. Across the five frames, frame 1 contains no masks at all, frames 2–4 capture the wearer's left and right arms reaching forward with the right hand below the hacksaw frame (which partially occludes the wooden board beneath it), and frame 5 loses the wearer's hands and saw entirely as they shift to the bottom-left edge while tracking the cat stretches diagonally upward in the upper right facing away from the wearer. While the segmentation masks sharply delineate the boundary of the wearer's limbs and the linear profile of the hacksaw frame in frames 2–3 relative to the cluttered floor in RGB, the map is highly unreliable overall. It completely misses the wooden board, hot-glue gun, white box, cardboard tubes, and floor layout across all frames, misclassifies the hacksaw frame as "scissors" in frames 2–3, and mislabels the cat in the upper right as "scissors" in frame 4 and "person" in frame 5 while hallucinating tiny "person" fragments on the upper-left floor in frame 2.
descriptions.pose: The body and hand skeleton map renders sparse 2D keypoints on a black background, capturing only fragments of the camera wearer's hands and right arm in the foreground (0.3 to 0.6 m from the viewpoint, within arm's reach) while no other people are present in the scene and the cat in the upper right (1.0 to 1.3 m away, facing away from the wearer) is appropriately excluded. In frame 1 no skeletons are detected; in frame 2 a magenta hand skeleton marks the wearer's right hand gripping the saw handle in the lower-right foreground; in frames 3 and 4 a yellow arm-like skeleton appears over the right hand and saw handle (with a magenta left hand skeleton also visible in frame 3 holding the wood on the left, about 0.25 m from the right hand); and in frame 5 a single magenta hand skeleton tracks the wearer's right hand after it moves to the bottom-left corner. The magenta hand skeletons in frames 2, 3, and 5 make the articulated finger positions and grip orientation on both the wooden workpiece and the saw handle easier to isolate than in the motion-blurred RGB frames. However, the pose map is unreliable in completeness and anatomical accuracy: it misses both hands in frame 1, the left hand in frames 2, 4, and 5, and the wearer's torso/legs entirely, while in frames 3 and 4 it hallucinated a miniature yellow body skeleton aligned with the held hacksaw and right forearm rather than the wearer's actual body layout.
